Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
PLAIN CLAMPS 

(First Revision ) 



( Reaffirmed 2005 ) 



1. Scope — Covers dimensions, material and other requirements for plain clamps used in holding work 
pieces in place when they are being machined, 

2. Dimensions — Shall be as given in Table 1. 

3. Designation — A plain clamp having £/== 14 mm and / = 80 mm shall be designated as: 

Plain Ciamp 14 x 80 IS : 6081 

4. Material — Steel suitably hardened and tempered to a tensile strength of 750 to 850 N/mm^ 

5. Finish — The pl^in clamps shall be free from cracks, burrs, pits and other defects. These shall also 
be free from sharp corners. 

6. Preservation and Packing 

6.1 A suitable anti-corrosive surface treatment shall be given to plain clamps. 

6.2 The plain clamps shall be packed in accordance with best trade practice. 

7. Marking 

7.1 The plain clamps shall be marked at an appropriate place with designation, manufacturer's name 
or trade-mark. 

7.2 IS! Certification Meriting — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. • 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1971. The committee responsible for formulation of this 
standard decided to revise the same to bring it in line with other standards on clamps, which are also 
being revised, in respect of material, roughness values, tolerance and rationalization of sizes. 

In the present revision, certain changes in dimensions in the plain clamp for screw size M20 
have been effected. Two more sizes of plain clamps have been included to suit screw sizes M24 
and M30. 



Adopted^ 29 May 1985 



O November 1985, BtS 



Gr 1 



BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS
